source_claims.statement: Source review of icon fetch (no SSRF due to controls). QR decode accepted SVG but returned 500. Shifted to migration/import path. AegisMigrator stored icon data without sanitization.
After QR decode failures, focused on POST /api/v1/twofaccounts/migration. Verified stored XSS with victim-goto headless browser.

research_questions.formulation: After QR-code SVG processing fails or is controlled, does the migration/import path store unsanitized icon data that is later rendered?
research_questions.anchor: shift from QrCodeController to AegisMigrator after 500s
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether imported icons are sanitized before storage
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that all SVG handling paths are equally protected

environment_model_updates: QR decode accepts SVG but errors
Migration stores Base64 icon data without sanitization

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: review of IconFetch, QR, and migration controllers
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: moving to migration after QR path failed

forbidden_inferences: Do not treat QR 500 as proof no SVG issues exist elsewhere
Stored XSS was in a different feature from the initial QR focus
next_evidence_actions: Note CVE-2024-52597; group with SRC-000021 under 2FAuth lineage
layer_b_candidate_principles: When one input path (QR decode) fails or is controlled, examine related import/migration features that handle the same data type
Stored content that is later rendered is a higher-value target than one-time processing endpoints
model_vs_harness: Recognizing migration as an alternative SVG sink is model reasoning; source review and headless verification can be partially harnessed.
